few visual adjustments to make to the board view:

1. the running indicator as should go to the corner of the card so it doesn't take too-much space, just indents the card name
2. the column width has a minimum threshold so on smaller screens there's a horizontal scrollbar
3. the card height is capped and long title is trimmed with ellipsis

Let's record these decisions under the respective cards in the #werk-board subtree and amend this prototype code

card vi-board  [decided]
A ticket board is a view beside the map, the graph, and the diagram
why: Tickets are units of build work, not decisions. A person reads them as columns to move through, not as a tree.
subtree: 6 cards, 6 decided, 1 unchallenged

A small board in the style of Trello. One column per ticket state, one card per ticket (#st-ticket). It follows the tickets through the whole run.

On the board, a ticket card shows only its title. Clicking a card opens a drawer beneath the board: the slice (often a few hundred words, since a real ticket brief is long) sits in a main column on the left, and the metadata and relations — the map cards it cites, what blocks it, retries, files, checks (#st-ticket's fields) — sit in a sidebar on the right. A click on a cited id in the sidebar opens that card on the map. A ticket that has retried more than once shows a small retry count next to its title.

A ticket with unmet blocked_by tickets shows a small count next to its title too, one per not-done ticket it depends on — the same kind of blocking-issue count Linear shows.

A building ticket with a live agent session pulses. It stops the moment the session ends, whether that is a pass, a failed retry waiting on the next attempt, or a person stopping the build by hand — pulsing means a session is running right now, not just that the ticket sits in building.

For a ticket currently in building, the drawer also shows a live preview of the agent's log, above the slice, in a fixed-height scrolling viewport. Moving out of building — forward or back to ready — drops the preview; it is a window onto a running session, not a permanent transcript.

The columns are in #werk-board-columns. What a person can do on the board is in #werk-board-control.

  -> refines         visual  The visual artifact is the primary medium
  -> depends_on      st-ticket  A ticket is a tracer-bullet slice of decided cards
       why: The board shows the tickets, their states and fields that #st-ticket defines.
  -> depends_on      st-iterative  Plan, build, and validate repeat in small slices
       why: The board follows tickets through the whole run because new tickets can join while other cards are still open.
  <- refines         werk-board-columns  The board follows the whole run, with one column per ticket state
  <- refines         werk-board-control  A person reorders, archives, triggers, and stops the build of one ticket at a time
  <- depends_on      werk-board  The ticket board in v0
  <- refines         vi-board-state  Ticket state is its own append-only log, .werk/board.jsonl, beside the decision log
  <- refines         vi-board-details  Board details: where archive and stop live, the run strip, and the live preview
  <- depends_on      werk-loop-state  Build state lives on tickets, not on cards
  <- depends_on      vi-flowtab  Flow is a fourth tab beside the graph, the diagram, and the board
  <- depends_on      vi-routes  Each view has its own address, so Back and Forward move between places in that view

card vi-board-state  [decided]
Ticket state is its own append-only log, .werk/board.jsonl, beside the decision log
why: A ticket is a unit of build work, not a decision (#st-ticket). Putting its moves in log.jsonl would mix build churn into the record of what was decided.

One event per line, in the same shape as the decision log. One pure fold turns it into the board, so the server, the command line and the build loop all read the board the same way.

Ticket events: planned, moved, reordered, archived, restored, build started, pass, build ended, merge, steps, held-out result.

Run events: tier, gate waiting, gate passed, run started, run ended. "Run started" names the merge-loop process that holds the run until "run ended". While that process is alive, the board's trigger joins the run instead of starting a second one (#werk-board-control).

A ticket id is <plan run>/<NN>. The ticket's text stays in .werk/tickets/<plan run>/<NN>.md; the boa

I changed the board view as you asked. I did not check it in a browser, so I have not seen the result on screen.

1. **Running dot:** the dot is now a 6px dot in the top-left corner of the ticket card. Only the first line of the title moves 5px to the right. A card with no running session looks the same as before.
2. **Column width:** each column is at least 200px wide (it was 150px). When five columns do not fit, the board gets a horizontal scrollbar.
3. **Card height:** a title shows two lines at most, then an ellipsis. When you hover over a cut title, it shows in full. The drawer header always shows the full title.

The change is in `web/style.css` and `web/board.js`. `npm run dev` reloads it.

**Three proposed cards wait for your ✓.** You have only my numbers for the first two:
- `#vi-board-pulse-corner` sits under #vi-board.
- `#vi-board-title-clamp` sits under #vi-board. I chose the two-line limit.
- `#werk-board-colwidth` sits under #werk-board-columns. I chose 200px.

#werk-board itself has no child cards. The board design cards are under #vi-board, so the new cards are there too.

Each card is decided. Each has the old behaviour as a rejected option, and a kill criterion that you test by hand. None of them has a `depends_on` edge, because the map refuses a `depends_on` link to a card's own parent. The card's place under its parent records that need, and each card is marked `--no-basis`.

**One stale card:** #werk-board-columns is already stale, from #st-build-run on 2026-09-25. `#werk-board-colwidth` depends only on how many columns there are, not on the merge steps, so that stale mark does not change it.
